title: Discovery of supersymmetry in nature and of how it is broken

concept.text: Strings 2000 problem 4 (proposed by Sergio Ferrara and Gordon Kane): is Nature supersymmetric, and if so, how is supersymmetry broken? Sources given: https://preskill.caltech.edu/millennium.html ; https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v54.i10.14_2.online.pdf ; https://x.com/martinmbauer/status/1779906631003697211.

change_log.change: Added by hand to PHY on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: One of the ten Physics Problems for the Next Millennium chosen at the Strings 2000 conference (University of Michigan) by a panel of Michael Duff, David Gross and Edward Witten; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: Supersymmetry and its breaking mechanism
page.definition: Supersymmetry would pair elementary particles whose spins differ by half a unit, relating integer-spin bosons to half-integer-spin fermions. An exact symmetry would give partners equal masses. The goal is to establish the symmetry experimentally and identify what breaks it, allowing the masses to differ. If the breaking originates in a hidden sector, this includes identifying how its effects reach the observed particles.

goal.need: Quantum corrections make the Higgs mass sensitive to physics at much higher energies. The pattern of superpartner masses would test whether cancellations keep the Higgs light without fine-tuning. In base ΛCDM cosmology, cold dark matter has about 5.4 times the density of ordinary matter. If a neutral superpartner is stable, its measured properties could be used to predict how much survived from the early universe. Identifying it as cosmic dark matter would also require evidence from searches for relic particles.

completion.title: Experiments establish supersymmetry and identify its breaking mechanism.
completion.criterion: Experimentally establish supersymmetry through superpartner spin, charge and coupling relations, then identify the dynamics that break the symmetry and the interactions that transmit the breaking to observed particles. The inferred mechanism must explain the measured mass splittings and interactions and be experimentally distinguishable from competing mechanisms.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; an operational interpretation of the Strings 2000 question and ILC reconstruction programme.
completion.basis: Searched the Strings 2000 problem list, ILC Reference Design Report §§5.1.3 and 5.3, and PDG’s experimental review for a published acceptance test for identifying the breaking mechanism; none was found. This test combines discovery with experimental identification of the breaking dynamics. A review first published on 21 July 2026 reports no conclusive evidence for supersymmetry.

milestones.title: A candidate superpartner is produced with a discovery significance of at least 5σ.
milestones.criterion: Observe a signal consistent with production of a candidate superpartner at a significance of at least 5σ against the background-only hypothesis.
milestones.set_by: Particle-physics discovery convention, stated by the ATLAS Collaboration in its glossary.
milestones.threshold_quote: Five sigma significance is traditionally required to claim a discovery of a new particle

milestones.title: New particles have the spins, charges and couplings required of Standard Model superpartners.
milestones.criterion: Determine spins, parity, gauge quantum numbers and couplings of the produced particles, and verify the supersymmetric relations to Standard Model particles. The roadmap supplies no universal measurement tolerance.
milestones.set_by: ILC Global Design Effort and World Wide Study, Reference Design Report, Volume 2, §5.1.3.
milestones.threshold_quote: their spin and parity, gauge quantum numbers and their couplings;

milestones.title: Measured superpartner properties determine the low-energy supersymmetry-breaking parameters.
milestones.criterion: Infer low-energy soft-breaking parameters—the mass and interaction terms that break supersymmetry—from measured superpartner masses, mixings and interactions, with minimal model assumptions. No universal precision is prescribed.
milestones.set_by: ILC Global Design Effort and World Wide Study, Reference Design Report, Volume 2, §§5.1.3 and 5.3.2.
milestones.threshold_quote: reconstruct the low–energy soft–SUSY breaking parameters

milestones.title: The masses and mixings of candidate superpartners are measured.
milestones.criterion: Determine the masses of the produced candidates and, for states that mix, determine their mixing from measurements of production and decay. Relevant observables include production cross sections, decay widths and branching fractions.
milestones.set_by: ILC Global Design Effort and World Wide Study, Reference Design Report, Volume 2, §5.1.3.
milestones.threshold_quote: measure the masses and mixings of the newly produced particles

milestones.title: Measured mass parameters test a predicted high-energy relation among superpartner masses.
milestones.criterion: Use the renormalization group equations of the theory under test to evolve the inferred low-energy mass parameters and their uncertainties to the scale specified by the model. Compare the resulting values with a predicted relation, such as equality of the mass parameters for the partners of the gauge bosons at a grand unification scale.
milestones.set_by: ILC Global Design Effort and World Wide Study, Reference Design Report, Volume 2, §§5.3.3–5.3.4.
milestones.threshold_quote: parameters from low to high scales are evolved
